conventions.testID: <scope>.<element>[.<part-or-key>...]: every segment [a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*, at least two segments. The scope is the route in kebab-case, an overlay (pause, result), a dialog (<name>-dialog), splash or consent. Interactive elements end in their role (-button, -switch, -slider, -row, -tile, -card, -segment). Repeated items append a stable data key (levels.level-tile.12, settings-language.language-row.fa), never a list index.
conventions.parts: A reusable component takes one testID and derives its parts by appending a segment: .icon .label .description .value .toggle .radio (ListRow), .icon .label .state (ToggleKey), .icon .label .description (RowButton), .back-button .title (TopBar), .tab .list (group), .number .stars-<n> .flag (LevelTile).
conventions.designSelector: Evaluated as frameElement.querySelectorAll(designSelector) on the unmodified design HTML after its script has run. ":scope" alone means the frame element itself. Must match exactly one element in the default render.
conventions.text: The copy-deck key of the visible text, or null for data (numbers, names, dates). games.<id>.<field>[.<n>|.<statKey>] is the current game's text; meta.languageNames.<lang> is an autonym.
conventions.a11yLabel: Copy-deck key of the accessible label when it is not the visible text (icon buttons, marks, charts). null means the deck has no key yet.
conventions.parent: The nearest listed ancestor with an accessible role (button, switch, radio, adjustable, image, alert). Maestro reports only that ancestor, so the part is crop-only (see reach).
conventions.a11yHidden: true for a decorative part its component hides from VoiceOver (IconTile, ArtTile, CalendarTile and its parts, LogoTile, PagerDots, PremiumArt, HazardStrip, the empty-stats Picture, decorative RatingStars, Confetti). Maestro's hierarchy omits hidden elements, so the part is crop-only (see reach). A screen never un-hides a decorative part to make it measurable.
conventions.coveredBy: For a crop-only element: the nearest reachable ancestor whose aligned crop the parity gates compare (crop or fill in its checks, or the frame root). The part's pixels, its text ink included, are judged inside that crop.
conventions.reach: One policy for VoiceOver and parity: bounds are checked only for elements Maestro lists (the frame root, containers, texts and accessible elements). Parts inside an accessible element (parent) and decorative parts hidden from VoiceOver (a11yHidden) are crop-only: checks is ["crop"] (or [] when parity hides them) and coveredBy names where they are compared.
conventions.requires: endless = only in games with an Endless mode (must be absent otherwise); no-endless = the opposite; game:<id> = its data key belongs to that game only (other games use their own key in the same place).
conventions.variants: The element exists only in these variants of the screen (default: every variant). One testID may appear in several entries of one screen with disjoint variants.
conventions.state: The state the design draws; the parity harness must put the app in the same state.
conventions.mask: Pixels are dynamic (ads, the game board): check geometry only.
conventions.when: The element exists only for games with these facts: hasMusic (the sound bank has music), winLine (moves or score) and hasHints (the rules give solver hints). The mockup draws hasMusic true, winLine moves and hasHints true; an element for other facts exists only in a design-derived reference variant (toybox-visual-parity).
conventions.surface: true for an accessible element drawn as the bottom layer of a card (a Pressable filling the card, like home.daily-card): the design nests the card's content in it, but the app draws that content above it as siblings. The texts on it are hidden from VoiceOver (a11yHidden, crop-only, coveredBy the surface, whose accessibility label carries them), and an accessible element on it (the Play key) is its own sibling, never its part.

checks.bounds: x, y, width, height of the element relative to the screen, within the parity tolerance (plus or minus 2 pt). Rotated elements compare their unrotated size and angle.
checks.text: The rendered text, whitespace-normalised, equals the design element's text.
checks.fill: The flat paint (background) colour, sampled from pixels on both sides, max channel difference 3.
checks.crop: Structural comparison of the element's pixel crop (icons, logos, stars, pictures, marks). For a crop-only element (parent or a11yHidden) the comparison happens inside the aligned crop of its coveredBy element.
